'''''Suaeda australis''''', the '''austral seablite''', is a species of plant in the family [[Amaranthaceae]],<ref name=apni/> native to [[Australia]].It was first described in 1810 by [[Robert Brown (botanist, born 1773)|Robert Brown]] as ''Chenopodium australe''.<ref name=apni/><ref>{{APNI2|id=63646|name=''Chenopodium australe''|access-date=2025-03-17}}</ref><ref>{{cite Q|Q7247677|pages=407|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/36315684}}</ref> In 1831 [[Alfred Moquin-Tandon]] transferred it to the genus, ''[[Suaeda]]'', to give its present name.<ref name="apni" /><ref>{{cite journal|lang=fr|author=Moquin-Tandon, C.H.B.A. |date=1831|journal= Annales des Sciences Naturelles| volume= 23| 
title=Rapport sur Le premier Mémoire sur la famille des Chenopodées, par M. Alfred Moquin, fait à l'Académie des Sciences| pages=318|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/6013190}}</ref> 

==Description==
It grows to {{convert|10|to|90|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} in height, with a spreading habit and branching occurring from the base. The leaves are up to 40 mm in length and are succulent, linear and flattened.<ref name=NSW>{{NSW Flora Online|author= Jacobs, S.W.L. |genus= Suaeda|species= australis}}</ref><ref name=FloraBase>{{FloraBase|name= ''Suaeda australis''|id=2639 }}</ref> They are light green to purplish-red in colour.<ref name=SA>{{cite web | url = http://www.flora.sa.gov.au/cgi-bin/texhtml.cgi?form=speciesfacts&family=Chenopodiaceae&genus=Suaeda&species=australis| title =''Suaeda australis'' | work = Electronic Flora of South Australia Fact Sheet | publisher = State Herbarium of South Australia }}</ref>

The species occurs on shorelines in coastal or estuarine areas or in [[salt marsh]]es. It is native across Australia including the states of [[Queensland]], [[New South Wales]], [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]], [[Tasmania]], [[South Australia]] and the south-west of [[Western Australia]].<ref name = NSW/>

In irrigated areas, the species is known as a salinity indicator plant and is referred to as '''redweed'''.<ref name=DPI>{{cite web|title=Austral Seablite|work=Victorian Resources Online|publisher=Department of Primary Industries (Victoria)|url=http://www.dpi.vic.gov.au/dpi/vro/vrosite.nsf/pages/water_sss_sea_blite}}</ref>
